scope: Repository-based research navigation, not a verified measure of national completeness.

statusDefinitions.partial: Public primary/secondary data exists, but important gaps remain
statusDefinitions.curated: Reviewed or attributed illustrative evidence, not an exhaustive sample
statusDefinitions.needs_data: Topic recognized; valid comparable dataset not yet established in the public Power Atlas corpus

items.title: Who draws the lines?
items.question: Trace maps, decision makers, litigation and election effects without assuming a connection proves intent.
items.gap: Complete historical state bills, court dockets, certified election returns and state judicial outcomes.

items.title: Who can cast a ballot?
items.question: Compare how ID and voting rules differ across states; separate statutes from secondary summaries.
items.gap: Independently version and verify state statutes, exceptions, implementation and turnout effects.

items.title: What happened in the 2026 elections?
items.question: Follow election outcomes, redistricting changes and the evidence behind competing explanations.
items.gap: Reconcile certified 2026 state and local returns before causal claims.

items.title: Which voters decided elections?
items.question: Examine pivotal voter groups across the 2018, 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2026 elections.
items.gap: Validated election survey microdata, consistent demographic crosswalks and uncertainty estimates.

items.title: What issues moved voters?
items.question: Compare voter issue preferences, party identification and candidate choice in competitive races.
items.gap: Matched polling microdata and race-level survey denominators; 2026 polls must be compared to outcomes.

items.title: Who finances federal campaigns?
items.question: Compare FEC cycle totals and distinguish receipts, spending, and potentially overlapping transfers.
items.gap: Final 2026 figures, state and local amounts, and reconciled entity-level payments.

items.title: Which donors appear in the top rankings?
items.question: Explore selected published top-40 midterm donor rankings, not a census of all donors.
items.gap: Full source-to-committee transaction paths and clearer individual-vs-household entity resolution.

items.title: Where does the money trail end?
items.question: Explore published committee receipts, investigative leads and undisclosed ultimate donors.
items.gap: Nationwide cross-jurisdiction itemized transfers and independent amendment review; hidden donors cannot be imputed.

items.title: Who is lobbying officials?
items.question: Review public lobbying filings and distinguish lobbying from proof of policy influence.
items.gap: Recipient/issue matching, LD-203 ledgers, outcome linkage and independent review.

items.title: Do officials' investments conflict with their votes?
items.question: Join legislator holdings/trades with dates of legislation and oversight roles.
items.gap: Official STOCK Act disclosures, transaction normalization, spouse/dependent handling and timing checks.

items.title: How could ordinary voters gain power?
items.question: Compare 16 reform proposals across transparency, structural safeguards, civic financing and enforcement.
items.gap: Effect estimates, local program evaluation and further legislative outcomes beyond the current casebook.

items.title: Do politicians represent constituents?
items.question: Study socioeconomic distance and voting alignment; observational links are not proof of motives.
items.gap: Validated district-survey linkages, wealth disclosures and causal identification.

items.title: Do elected officials keep promises?
items.question: Compare documented promises with the limited officially reviewable evidence of follow-through.
items.gap: Exhaustive pledge denominators and independent promise adjudication.

items.title: When do institutions lose trust?
items.question: Compare accountability, service quality and public trust across carefully scoped observations.
items.gap: Comparable repeated-wave observations and independently powered causal designs.

items.title: How divided has Congress become?
items.question: Inspect roll-call divisions, party gaps, cross-party cooperation and productivity.
items.gap: Correct noncausal interpretation and additional party-vote linkage beyond bounded periods.

items.title: How does political identity affect cooperation?
items.question: Separate partisan identity, behavior, rhetoric and competing explanations of polarization.
items.gap: Individual-level panel datasets, validated content coding and causal design.

items.title: Do political tactics differ across groups?
items.question: Compare reported actions by identical event definitions, category filters and crowd-size scale.
items.gap: A licensed U.S. event-level ACLED or comparable protest dataset, deduplication and independent classification.

items.title: How does concentrated wealth change prices?
items.question: Test pricing power, housing costs, market concentration and policy transmission mechanisms.
items.gap: Antitrust, industry prices and transaction data; causal counterfactuals instead of assuming billionaire ownership caused price increases.

items.title: Which policies helped or harmed Americans since 1969?
items.question: Compare outcomes across administrations without attributing all trends to the party in office.
items.gap: Detailed policy dates, matched counterfactuals, economic controls and methodology for mixed effects.

items.title: What have officials actually done about political influence?
items.question: Follow official bills, public votes, enforcement examples and actual local programs.
items.gap: Exhaustive bill-event histories, complete voting records and enacted-versus-proposed monitoring.

items.title: Who appoints or elects the judges?
items.question: Follow federal judicial appointments and the state judicial-selection process when redistricting cases are decided.
items.gap: State judicial-election funding, appointment processes and complete lower-court dockets; appointments do not imply coordinated outcomes.

items.title: Who is connected to political decisions?
items.question: Map public committee memberships, lobbying filings, officials and organizational relationships without inventing a money trail.
items.gap: Source-confirmed individual funding edges, identity adjudication and decision-level chronology.

items.title: Are elections equally accessible in practice?
items.question: Assess registration and roll purges, early and mail voting, felony eligibility, polling-site access and administrative burden.
items.gap: Versioned primary state administrative records, county-level polling sites, purge notices, eligibility remedies and measured implementation.

items.title: Does political outrage raise more money?
items.question: Test whether viral confrontation, strategic outrage and partisan rhetoric correlate with fundraising and primary survival.
items.gap: Timestamped public speeches, content coding, engagement measures, matched FEC contributions and credible causal controls.

items.title: What helps opposing groups cooperate?
items.question: Study constructive dialogue, shared incentives and institutional conditions for cooperation on energy, climate, debt, health and conflict.
items.gap: Representative cross-group experiments, demographic controls, follow-up measures and validated cross-country replication.

evidenceRules: A source link is not an ingested dataset.
A recorded payment, membership or vote is not proof of illegal influence.
Unverified, missing and legally undisclosed data are distinct.
Do not use political-party identity to define extremism or assign guilt.
Compare like-for-like denominators and distinct reporting windows.
Legislative proposals are not enacted law; observational relationships are not causal findings.
